title: Spec: message envelope, content model, and versioning
body:
**Source:** DESIGN Preliminary message envelope; PLANNING-PROMPT §9.6

## Outcome
Normative definition of the envelope: `version`, `id`, `from`, `to`, `conversation_id`, `reply_to`, `correlation_id`, `created_at`, `ttl_ms`, `content`, `security`. Plus the protocol versioning and compatibility policy.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Every field MUST/SHOULD/MAY qualified, with types and cardinality
- [ ] Trusted `security` metadata is structurally distinguishable from user- and model-controlled `content`
- [ ] Text content type only for v0.1; extension points defined without implying attachments
- [ ] TTL and expiry semantics defined
- [ ] Versioning policy states what a minor revision may change and what forces a new extension identifier
- [ ] No provider or transport name appears anywhere in this document

**Skills:** `oac-spec-authoring`, `oac-boundaries`

title: Spec: session identity, addressing, and capability negotiation
body:
**Source:** DESIGN Addressing; PLANNING-PROMPT §5.3, §5.4

## Outcome
Normative addressing and capability model: opaque stable session ids, the display form, human aliases, `SessionDescriptor`, `SessionCapabilities`, and extension/version negotiation.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Ids are opaque, stable, and bound to a device key; transport-native addresses are never exposed
- [ ] Display form and human aliases are explicitly non-authoritative
- [ ] Capability set includes whether active inbound is supported
- [ ] Negotiation defined including what a peer MUST do on an unknown version
- [ ] Unsupported-capability behaviour is defined, not implied

**Skills:** `oac-spec-authoring`

title: Spec: active delivery, presence, discovery, and the no-polling rule
body:
**Source:** DESIGN Presence/discovery, Delivery semantics; ADR-001 Decision

## Outcome
The normative concept — a harness advertising active inbound support accepts an authorized external channel message as input to the addressed live session without application-level polling — plus presence and discovery.

## Acceptance
- [ ] The active-inbound obligation stated normatively
- [ ] Presence states start at `online`, `unreachable`, `unknown`; provider-specific activity states are not over-normalized
- [ ] Discovery answers: which sessions are reachable, which harness owns them, their capabilities, and whether active inbound is supported
- [ ] Provider-supported streaming connections, subscriptions, event loops, and keepalives are explicitly allowed; application-level inbox polling is explicitly forbidden for adapters claiming active inbound

**Skills:** `oac-spec-authoring`, `oac-boundaries`

title: Spec: delivery receipts, replies, correlation, and the error taxonomy
body:
**Source:** DESIGN Delivery semantics; conflicts C6 and C9

## Outcome
Delivery states, reply and correlation rules, acknowledgement and error semantics.

## Acceptance
- [ ] States cover at least `accepted`, `rejected`, `unreachable`, `expired`, `duplicate`, `failed`, each defined by what is actually knowable
- [ ] Exactly-once delivery is explicitly not promised; ids, idempotency, and duplicate suppression are required instead
- [ ] A receipt never claims the model saw a message when the provider gives no acknowledgement
- [ ] Reply and correlation rules work for a provider with no channel-tag convention
- [ ] Error taxonomy is closed: every error a conformant peer may emit is enumerated

**Skills:** `oac-spec-authoring`

title: Spec: security document — identity, signing, replay, authorization, provenance
body:
**Source:** DESIGN Security; PLANNING-PROMPT §7, §9.7

## Outcome
`spec/security.md`: the normative security model, independent of any transport's own security features.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Identity hierarchy normative: security principal -> device -> harness -> session
- [ ] Signature algorithm, signed field set, and verification procedure are normative (transport-layer security is not accepted as a substitute)
- [ ] Replay window, nonce, and duplicate-suppression requirements normative
- [ ] Default deny; authorization decision points named
- [ ] Provenance rendering requirements stated neutrally, with per-provider realization left to adapters
- [ ] Authenticated peer messages are declared untrusted instruction content that may carry prompt injection

**Skills:** `oac-spec-authoring`, `oac-security-work`

title: Spec: MCP extension binding document
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §3.3, §5.3

## Outcome
A separate binding document describing how OAC is carried over MCP: the extension identifier, the tool surface, `_meta` provenance keys, and the dual-era constraint.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Kept out of the neutral spec so that MCP is one binding, not the protocol
- [ ] States that no MCP revision defines 'external event becomes a user turn'; that semantic is always provider-native
- [ ] `_meta` key prefixes conform to the spec's prefix rules
- [ ] Legacy-era and current-era behaviour both described, with the G4 result cited

**Skills:** `oac-spec-authoring`, `oac-mcp`, `oac-boundaries`

title: Freeze the adapter contract, transport contract, and core types
body:
**Source:** DESIGN Provider adapter contract, Transport contract, Core; PLANNING-PROMPT §8 Stage 2

## Outcome
Frozen interfaces: `ProviderAdapter` (`discover_sessions`, `attach`, `deliver`, `publish_output`, `capabilities`, `health`, `shutdown`), `Transport` (`start`, `publish`, `subscribe`, `announce_presence`, `watch_presence`, `health`, `shutdown`), and the core neutral types.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Adapters route through core policy and security, never directly to a transport
- [ ] Optional transport capabilities (reliability, persistence, offline queueing, ordering, multicast discovery, routing/federation) are declared, not assumed
- [ ] Core types cover `SessionIdentity`, `SessionDescriptor`, `SessionCapabilities`, `ChannelMessage`, `DeliveryReceipt`, `PresenceRecord`, `SecurityPrincipal`, and authorization decisions
- [ ] No provider or transport concept appears in any signature; any unavoidable exception is documented with its reason
- [ ] Freeze is explicit: later changes need a recorded amendment

**Skills:** `oac-spec-authoring`, `oac-boundaries`

title: Build the conformance fixture set
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §8 Stage 2, §9.10

## Outcome
Language-independent fixtures that any implementation can run to claim conformance: valid and invalid envelopes, signature vectors, replay and duplicate cases, and expected delivery-state outcomes.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Fixtures are data files, not code, and are readable by a second implementation
- [ ] Each fixture names the spec clause it proves
- [ ] Negative fixtures cover forged signatures, expired timestamps, replayed nonces, and unknown versions
- [ ] A conformance runner exists and is wired into CI in Stage 3

**Skills:** `oac-spec-authoring`, `oac-testing`

title: Write the design-for-replacement proofs
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §6

## Outcome
Proofs argued from the frozen interfaces, not from prose.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A third provider adapter — ACP as the worked example — can be added with no change to any transport module, shown by walking the interfaces
- [ ] NATS or MQTT can replace Zenoh with no change to any adapter or to the spec, with the optional capabilities each candidate lacks listed
- [ ] The transport contract is documented well enough for an independent second backend (DESIGN acceptance criterion 10)
- [ ] ACP is characterized correctly as a client-owned-session protocol, not a channel

**Skills:** `oac-spec-authoring`, `oac-boundaries`

title: Scaffold the repository workspace and module boundaries
body:
**Source:** DESIGN Suggested repository shape; PLANNING-PROMPT §9.8

## Outcome
The workspace: `spec/`, `core/`, `cli/`, `transports/zenoh/`, `adapters/claude/`, `adapters/codex/`, `tests/{protocol,security,integration}/`, `examples/`, `docs/`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Dependency direction enforced by the build: adapters and transports depend on core; core depends on neither
- [ ] Provider and transport crates cannot be reached from core
- [ ] Apache-2.0 headers and license inventory tooling in place
- [ ] Builds clean on Windows, macOS, and Linux

**Skills:** `oac-implementation`

title: Implement core neutral types and envelope serialization
body:
## Outcome
The frozen core types and envelope encode/decode with strict validation.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Round-trips every positive conformance fixture
- [ ] Rejects every negative fixture with the specified error
- [ ] Unknown fields handled per the versioning policy
- [ ] Trusted security metadata cannot be populated from content-derived input by construction

**Skills:** `oac-implementation`, `oac-testing`

title: Implement device identity, key storage, signing, and verification
body:
## Outcome
Device key generation and storage in the OS credential store with an encrypted-file fallback, plus envelope signing and verification over the normative field set.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Works on Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, and Linux Secret Service, with the fallback exercised on a headless Linux box
- [ ] Signature vectors from the conformance set pass
- [ ] Private key material never leaves the process that owns it, and never appears in logs or receipts
- [ ] Ephemeral harness and session identities are bound to the device key

**Skills:** `oac-implementation`, `oac-security-work`

title: Implement replay defence and duplicate suppression
body:
## Outcome
Timestamp window, nonce tracking, and the duplicate-suppression store.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Replayed envelopes rejected inside and outside the window, with the correct delivery state
- [ ] Duplicate message ids suppressed idempotently
- [ ] Store is bounded; eviction policy stated and tested
- [ ] Behaviour across process restart is defined and tested

**Skills:** `oac-implementation`, `oac-security-work`

title: Implement the authorization engine and pairing store
body:
## Outcome
Default-deny policy evaluation, per-session sender allowlists, and the pairing store for same-device and LAN pairing.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Denies by default with no configuration present
- [ ] Same-user multi-harness pairing on one device requires no configuration
- [ ] LAN pairing requires an explicit short code or file exchange
- [ ] Authorization decisions are logged with the principal, never with the message body
- [ ] A session in one working directory is not discoverable by an unauthorized peer

**Skills:** `oac-implementation`, `oac-security-work`

title: Implement the presence registry and delivery receipt state machine
body:
## Outcome
Session registration, presence states, and the receipt state machine with honest 'unknown' handling.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Presence transitions between `online`, `unreachable`, `unknown` are tested including expiry
- [ ] Receipts distinguish 'accepted by adapter', 'handed to harness', and 'unknown'
- [ ] No path can produce a receipt asserting model visibility on a provider that gives no acknowledgement
- [ ] Presence survives individual session exit per the chosen process model

**Skills:** `oac-implementation`

title: Implement the in-memory transport
body:
## Outcome
A loopback transport implementing the frozen transport contract, used by every CI-default test.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Implements the contract with no Zenoh dependency
- [ ] Can inject reordering, loss, duplication, and delay for test purposes
- [ ] Declares its optional capabilities honestly
- [ ] Passes the transport contract suite

**Skills:** `oac-implementation`, `oac-testing`

title: Build the fake Claude Code channel endpoint from recorded fixtures
body:
## Outcome
A fake harness endpoint that replays the D6 Claude fixtures, including legacy negotiation, notification delivery, mid-turn queueing, and tool replies.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Reproduces the no-acknowledgement behaviour faithfully
- [ ] Reproduces mid-turn queue-then-deliver-in-order behaviour
- [ ] Silently drops non-identifier-safe `meta` keys, as the real harness does
- [ ] Requires no Claude Code install, no API key, and no network beyond loopback

**Skills:** `oac-testing`, `oac-claude-channels`

title: Build the fake Codex app-server endpoint from recorded fixtures
body:
## Outcome
A fake JSON-RPC app-server replaying the D6 Codex fixtures over stdio and WebSocket.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Implements `initialize`/`initialized`, thread and turn methods, and the event stream including `item/completed` and `turn/completed`
- [ ] Models queued-until-idle behaviour for `thread/queue/add`
- [ ] Models the experimental-API capability gate
- [ ] Requires no Codex install, no OpenAI credential, and no network beyond loopback

**Skills:** `oac-testing`, `oac-codex-appserver`

title: Write the adapter and transport contract test suites
body:
## Outcome
Reusable suites that any adapter or transport implementation must pass, driven by the frozen contracts.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Adapter suite runs against both fakes and, later, against the real adapters unchanged
- [ ] Transport suite runs against the in-memory transport and, later, against Zenoh unchanged
- [ ] Suites assert the no-polling rule for adapters claiming active inbound
- [ ] Suites assert that adapters route through core policy rather than straight to a transport

**Skills:** `oac-testing`

title: Write the security test suite against the fakes
body:
## Outcome
Spoofing, replay, unauthorized-routing, and provenance tests that run with no live provider.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A message whose content claims another sender fails to change rendered provenance
- [ ] Forged and altered signatures are rejected
- [ ] Replayed and duplicated envelopes produce the specified states
- [ ] An unauthorized peer cannot discover or address a session
- [ ] Each test names the threat-table row it proves

**Skills:** `oac-testing`, `oac-security-work`

title: Stand up CI: default tier green with no providers
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §6, §9.10

## Outcome
CI running unit, conformance, contract, security, and fake-integration tiers on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Default pipeline uses no live provider, no API key, and no network beyond loopback
- [ ] Provider integration tests exist but are opt-in and pinned
- [ ] The Zenoh-containment check runs as a build-failing lint
- [ ] License inventory check runs and fails on an unapproved license

**Skills:** `oac-implementation`, `oac-testing`
